samples.summary: Public REST docs still describe the pre-change freeze/merges contract
samples.evidence: `packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:653` says of `PUT .../freeze`: "Both default to `0` when absent, so `PUT {}` unfreezes. `GET` returns `{ "rows", "cols" }`" — with no mention that the PUT now snaps past a merged block it would cut and answers with a boundary that may be larger than the one sent (worksheet.controller.ts:104-120). The merged-cells section at :671-685 documents `PUT merges` with no mention of the new 409, and the refusal table at :631 lists only "Merge split (move only) | `409`", while :563 states the move rule as split-only. An API client that stores the value it sent, or that treats 409 on `PUT merges` as unexpected, is now out of step with the server.

samples.summary: Design doc's API-vs-editor difference list omits the two new refusals and the freeze snap
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:314 still reads "**A move that would split a merged range returns `409`.**" as the only merge-related deliberate difference. The branch adds a second 409 on `POST .../move` (block landing across the freeze), a 409 on `PUT .../merges`, and a silently-grown freeze on `POST insert`/`POST delete` and `PUT freeze` — all documented in the controller docstrings and in docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:130-144, but not here.

samples.summary: CLI help text and CLI docs describe the move 409 as split-only
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-structure.ts:185 — the `move` command description ends "...; 409 if the move would split a merged range", and the file docstring at :33 repeats it. packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:559 has the same table row. The endpoint now also 409s when the reorder would park a merged block across the frozen boundary (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:168-204), so the user-facing help under-describes when the command fails.

samples.summary: shiftWorksheetViewState's "safe in both places" docstring assumes an unconditional freeze re-write that Sheet no longer performs
samples.evidence: worksheet-structure.ts:182-186 justifies applying the view-state shift in both the store helper and `Sheet` with: "`Sheet` persists these fields by assigning the whole value it computed … so the editor's later write is the same value again." After this change `Sheet.shiftCells` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1424-1429) calls `store.setFreezePane` only when the value differs from `frozenBefore`, so the editor no longer unconditionally reasserts the boundary over whatever `applyWorksheetShift` wrote into the Yorkie doc. The two computations should agree, but the comment's stated safety argument no longer holds as written, and any divergence (e.g. the in-memory merge map lagging the doc's) would now persist instead of being overwritten.

samples.summary: Concurrency fuzz driver ignores the new move refusal signal
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/test/helpers/concurrency-driver.ts:52-56 does `await sheet.moveRows(op.src, op.count, op.dst)` / `moveColumns(...)` and discards the result. `moveCells` can now decline a scheduled op (merged block landing across a freeze) based on each replica's local freeze/merge state, so a generated op can be applied on one replica and silently dropped on another while the driver records it as executed — weakening exactly the convergence signal this harness exists to give.

samples.summary: Move-side freeze guard duplicated at both call sites instead of living in applyWorksheetMove, unlike the shift-side snap
samples.evidence: The shift repair was deliberately placed in the shared helper (`shiftWorksheetViewState`, worksheet-structure.ts:271-288) "so every caller of `applyWorksheetShift` upholds the same invariant". The move-side equivalent was not: `applyWorksheetMove` (worksheet-structure.ts:620) has no freeze check, and the invariant is enforced separately in `Sheet.moveCells` (sheet.ts:1548-1558) and in `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController.assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:182-204). Today those are the only two callers, so nothing is broken; a third caller (a restore/replay path, a future service) would reach `applyWorksheetMove` without the guard and persist a straddling block.
searchedFor: grep applyWorksheetMove across repo (backend controller + frontend yorkie-store.ts:512 only)

samples.summary: Store-level setFreezePane writes bypass the new snap
samples.evidence: `Sheet.setFreezePane` now snaps past merged blocks, but `Store.setFreezePane` does not, and the visual harness writes freeze straight through the store: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/sheet-scenarios.tsx:117 (`store.setFreezePane(1, 1)`) and :333 (`store.setFreezePane(2, 0)`), alongside `store.setMerge(...)` at :230. Harness-only today, so no product impact, but it is the one in-repo path that can seed the straddling state the engine now refuses to create.
searchedFor: grep setFreezePane across packages/frontend and packages/sheets src
